subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, and which parts should instead live in plugins, SDK seams, or ClawHub?
rationale: The safety goal fits current priorities, but implementation touches storage policy, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, doctor/runtime guardrails, and core-vs-plugin boundaries that need maintainer intent before repair work is safe to queue.

options.title: Core guardrails plus SQLite seam
options.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving workflow-specific classification to plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Core would own temp artifact classes, persistence, and cleanup/janitor semantics for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts.

options.title: Plugin-only workflow scope
options.body: Core would keep existing temp-root hardening while workflow-specific audit/review provenance remains a ClawHub or plugin package concern.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus SQLite seam
recommendation.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving workflow-specific classification to plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest combination of recent temp-boundary history, product-scope review context, and prior related scope decision evidence.
